title: console-decision-tree-walkthrough-notes-may2026
content:
Purpose: quick capture from moderated walkthrough sessions (remote) testing a new decision-tree flow for creating routing and fallback policies in the Console. We wanted to validate mental models, label clarity, and whether a compact, stepwise wizard reduces errors compared to the current freeform policy editor.

Participants: 6 product engineers and 4 SREs from early access customers (names withheld per NDA), 3 internal SEs who performed customer scenarios. Sessions: two 45-minute moderated walkthroughs + unmoderated remote prototype for 20 external participants over 72 hours.

Test scenarios (high-level):
- Create a new routing policy that prefers low-cost model variants in region A and falls back to high-availability variants in region B after 250ms latency.
- Edit an existing rollout so that canary traffic is sent to a quantized variant when token length & burst conditions are met.
- Diagnose a route failure and add an auto-fallback to a CPU-based endpoint without losing route-level observability.

Tasks given to participants (short):
1) "Create policy: cost-first then HA fallback with 250ms threshold"
2) "Add condition: route uses quantized model only when average sequence < 512 tokens"
3) "Simulate a region outage and configure automatic cross-region fallback while preserving logs"

Observations and behavioral notes (ranked by frequency):
1) Onboarding friction: participants expected a single place to name + preview the policy before configuring low-level knobs. The stepwise wizard split name/preview into step 1 and step 4; 5/10 testers missed the confirmation step and left intermediate drafts. (Severity: medium)
2) Mental model mismatch: testers used the term "route" and "policy" interchangeably; the UI presents them separately. Customers asked for clearer mapping (e.g., "Routing policy for Route <name>"). (Severity: medium-high)
3) Latency threshold phrasing: several users read "250ms latency" as an average rather than a p95 SLA. UI should clarify percentile. (Severity: high)
4) Conditional rules UX: building compound conditions (token length + time window + request tag) felt clunky; users wanted copy/paste of previous conditions and multi-row visualization instead of nested indents. (Severity: high)
5) Real-time preview: the model variant preview showed fictional metadata; participants wanted to run a 3-token dry-run to see estimated cost and percent change relative to baseline. (Severity: medium)
6) Error recovery flow: when a rule produced an incompatible policy (e.g., selecting quantized 4-bit model for unsupported ops), the console presented a generic error. Users wanted guidance: "why not supported" and suggested automatic suggestions for compatible fallback. (Severity: high)

Direct quotes (anonymized):
- "I don’t know whether I’m setting a rule on the route or on the policy — it looks like both are changing."
- "Show me the expected cost before I save. I can’t risk flipping this on without a quick estimate."
- "Nesting these conditions makes it hard to audit later — give me a flattened view for quick reading."

Wireframe writeup (low-fidelity summary):
- Landing: contextual header that shows Route name + quick metrics (p50/p95 latency, current cost burn rate). CTA: New Routing Policy -> opens decision-tree wizard.
- Step 1: Name & preview panel (single-line name, description, dry-run button that returns token estimate and delta).
- Step 2: Selector matrix for primary route targets (picker: model variant, region, capacity tier). Each cell includes inline microcopy about cost and whether variant supports the requested ops.
- Step 3: Condition builder (flat rows, each row = one conditional expression, with inline AND/OR toggles). Offer "copy previous" and "convert to group" to reduce repeated clicks.
- Step 4: Fallback and observability (select fallback targets, retention window for traces, and toggle to export alerts to PagerDuty/Slack).
- Final: Save & Test (runs a dry-run and gives quick pass/warn/fail with suggestions).

Accessibility & labeling notes:
- Add percentile qualifiers to latency labels (p50/p95) everywhere.
- Ensure keyboard-first traversal for the condition builder; support ARIA live region for dry-run feedback.

Backlog candidates (prioritized quick list):
- A: Rename step header + show single-line preview earlier (JIRA: RINF-2134) — quick win, low complexity.
- B: Add percentile suffix to latency fields and tooltip microcopy (RINF-2135) — trivial.
- C: Implement flat-condition builder with copy/convert actions (RINF-2201) — medium complexity, high impact.
- D: Dry-run cost estimator (3-token test against selected variants) with delta to baseline (RINF-2198) — needs infra support; spike required.
- E: Contextual incompatibility hints when a variant doesn't support requested ops + suggested fallback (RINF-2210) — medium-high complexity.
- F: Add export toggle to route failures to PagerDuty & include runbook link (RINF-2211) — low-medium.

Open questions / unknowns: 
- Can the backend return a lightweight dry-run cost and ops-compatibility check without requiring full inference? Need input from serving-runtime (ENG: Samir) and infra.
- How will rollout metrics (cost delta over time) be surfaced for saved policies vs transient dry-runs? Product decision needed.
- Do customers want versioning for policies (save as draft, publish, rollback)? Several team members asked for a history/rollback surface.

Next steps (near term):
- Action 1 (this week): implement microcopy changes (percentiles + header preview) and a small layout tweak so name/preview appears before conditions. Owner: Lena Ortiz.
- Action 2 (this sprint): scope spike for dry-run API with serving-runtime & infra. Owner: Samir Gupta. Deliverable: API contract + cost estimate for 2-week implementation.
- Action 3 (next planning): groom RINF-2201 (flat-condition builder) with design comps and UX acceptance criteria. Owner: Maya Singh.

Attachments / art: low-fi png sketches in prototype: /drive/prototypes/console-decision-tree/lowfi-frames.png (see linked_artifacts). For the record: screenshots of the current editor used in tests are saved under test-captures/test-05-04.zip.

Quick take: participants liked the idea of a guided flow but need immediate preview of the policy effects (cost + latency percentile semantics) and a flatter, copy-first condition builder to make rule authoring tolerable at scale. Prioritize dry-run and condition builder features next; microcopy fixes can be shipped as low-risk first patch.

Notes on privacy: external participant quotes are anonymized and stored with consent in research vault.

Document owner: Maya R. Singh (product-console).
